description: The team consists of students from the KPI Institute of Aerospace Technologies
summary:
To address the critical hazards of combustion in microgravity, we developed "Flame in Freefall", a hybrid AI-powered interactive dashboard designed for autonomous offline operation on spacecraft. Utilizing data from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository (including SAFFIRE, FLEX, and BASS-II experiments), our solution features a statistical surrogate heatmap that visualizes flammability probability based on oxygen concentration, flow speed, pressure, and gravity levels.

Our tool addresses the challenge by transforming raw combustion data into an actionable ranking system for spacecraft materials, dynamically assessing risks for ISS, Lunar, and Martian environments. Furthermore, we integrated a local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI assistant capable of running on onboard GPU hardware, ensuring astronauts have instant, offline access to fire safety protocols. This is crucial because fire behaves unpredictably in space—such as forming spherical cool flames—and relying on Earth-based connectivity during an emergency is too slow.
details:
What it does and how it works: "Flame in Freefall" is a hybrid AI dashboard designed to assess and mitigate fire hazards in microgravity and partial gravity environments. Developed using Python (Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, Plotly), our solution translates raw combustion data into an interactive statistical surrogate heatmap. This heatmap dynamically visualizes the probability of sustained combustion across various oxygen levels, ventilation flow speeds, pressures, and gravity conditions (ISS, Moon, Mars). It also features an evidence-based material ranking system that evaluates spacecraft materials based on adjustable safety criteria (Impact, Evidence, Mission Fit).

Creativity and Factors Considered: Earth-based fire safety standards (1g) fail in space, where flames can become spherical, undergo radiative quenching, or leave invisible cool flames. Our team recognized that deep space missions (like Artemis or Mars surface habitats) will suffer from severe Earth-to-space communication latency. Therefore, we designed our architecture to be 100% autonomous. We integrated a local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI assistant concept, designed to run entirely offline on onboard edge GPUs (such as repurposed hardware like Nvidia GTX series).

Intended Impact: This tool provides astronauts with instant, data-driven, life-saving protocols during an emergency without waiting for Earth connectivity, bridging the gap between complex NASA combustion physics and practical crew safety.
